title: Textbooks without the sticker shock
description: New textbooks can cost a fortune — here are the legal, cheaper routes students actually use.

body.heading: Check before you buy
paragraphs: Before buying anything, check the reading list carefully: some books are needed for one chapter, and the library may hold copies or an e-book version included in your course.
Ask students from the year above which books they actually used. Honest answers can save you from the classic mistake — buying every listed book in week one.

body.heading: Second-hand and sharing
paragraphs: Used copies, older editions, and library reserve shelves cover most needs at a fraction of the price. Check with your teacher whether an older edition is acceptable; often the changes are minor.
Sharing a copy with a study partner, or splitting a set between a small group, works well for reference books you consult rather than read cover to cover.

body.heading: Sell on when done
paragraphs: If you do buy, keep books in good condition and sell them on when the course ends. Your discount this year becomes someone else's next year.

takeaway: Check the library and older students first — most textbook needs have a cheaper route.
